subject: [hw] T01 -> V14: LSRS/ASRS register shift by 0 root cause: t16_shift() treats n==0 as 32 for both register and immediate
body:
Found the exact cause in emu/n2a32_t16.c: t16_shift() lines ~121-146 do `if (n == 0) n = 32;` for LSR/ASR. That is correct for the **immediate** forms (LSR #0 encodes #32) but wrong for the **register** forms (case 0x3/0x4 in the data-processing register decoder pass `y & 0xFF`): a register-specified shift of 0 leaves the value unchanged and C unchanged, it is not a shift of 32. Your comment at line 96 already says the difference. Repro stays:
  movs r0,#0x5a; movs r1,#0; lsrs r0,r1  -> got 0, want 0x5a
  same asrs; lsls is correct.
Suggested minimal fix: add an `immediate` flag (or separate helper) so the `n==0 -> 32` conversion only happens for the immediate path; for the register path, n==0 must fall through to the existing `n==0 -> r=x, carry unchanged, N/Z set if sf` behavior. Corpus: 35 mismatches at thumb-O0 = k_crc32 15 + k_v15_rev 20; thumb-O2/O3v are now 0 mismatches after V15 fixes, so this is the only remaining T16 mismatch. No action needed on the flag letter beyond that.
